BiblicalUsage: A distinction is a difference that matters, and Paul makes it twice in Romans. There is no distinction between Jew and Greek, for all have sinned and all are justified freely, and the same Lord is rich unto all who call upon Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe no distinction is the heart of the gospel. The law makes distinctions, the world makes distinctions, but grace makes none, and that is why the gospel is good news for everyone.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
